_meta.note: CURATED ENGINEERING DEFAULTS, hand-maintained. Edit freely.
_meta.authority: adapy. This file is NOT part of the DEXPI specification, is not derived from it, and carries no DEXPI authorship -- unlike the generated dexpi_classes.json next to it, which is. The only thing shared with the spec is the class names used as keys.
_meta.purpose: A P&ID says what an item is, never how big it is or where its nozzles sit. These are plausible starting sizes so a DEXPI import can be laid out and routed; they are placeholders for real vendor data, not engineering deliverables. Override per tag or per class with an equipment definition list (ada.cadit.dexpi.equipment_list).
_meta.bbox: [lx, ly, lz]: the equipment-local envelope. The local origin is the footprint centre at the base, so the box spans x in [-lx/2, lx/2], y in [-ly/2, ly/2], z in [0, lz] -- the same frame ada.Equipment ports use.
_meta.ifc: IFC4 element class the equipment is written as.
_meta.nozzles: Nozzle-layout strategy, resolved by ada.cadit.dexpi.nozzle_placers.PLACERS. Nozzle POSITIONS are generated per item from its actual DEXPI nozzles, never fixed per class -- the count varies item by item.
_meta.density: Apparent envelope density in kg/m3 (dry and empty, mass over the whole bbox, not the material density). Mass = density * lx * ly * lz, so an overridden bbox still gets a proportionate mass. An entry may instead give an explicit 'mass' in kg, which wins and does not scale.
_meta.resolution: Looked up by DEXPI class name; a class with no entry of its own inherits the nearest entry up its supertype DAG (ada.cadit.dexpi.class_table.is_a). 'ProcessEquipment' is the catch-all for the 142 Plant/ProcessEquipment classes, so a few dozen entries answer for all of them. Chamber and Nozzle do NOT derive from ProcessEquipment (both come straight off Core/ConceptualObject), hence Chamber's own entry.

Agitator.note: Drive plus shaft standing on its vessel; the mounting nozzle is the vessel's, not the agitator's.

Blower.note: Packaged blower on a skid: side suction, top discharge, same layout as a pump.

Centrifuge.note: Horizontal decanter; heavy for its size because the bowl and drive dominate the mass.

Chamber.note: A sub-volume of its owner (a separator boot, a jacket). Normally folded into the owning equipment; sized only for the case where it is materialised on its own.

Compressor.note: Machine, driver and baseplate as one envelope.

CoolingTower.note: Induced-draught cell: a large, mostly empty air volume, so the envelope density is low.

ElectricGenerator.note: Copper and laminations in a compact frame.

Filter.note: Vertical cartridge/bag housing: a pressure vessel with an inlet, an outlet and a drain.

HeatExchanger.note: Long in X so the two ends of the exchanger strategy fall on the +/-X faces.

Heater.note: Fired heater / package boiler; refractory carries much of the mass.

Mill.note: Crushers and grinders are the densest process items on a plant -- cast bodies and grinding media.

Mixer.note: Agitated vessel: feeds on top, product out of the bottom.

MobileTransportSystem.note: A road tanker/waggon envelope, present on a P&ID as a loading interface.

Motor.note: The densest common item: an iron and copper block with no void.

PlateHeatExchanger.note: A plate pack is tall and thin where a shell-and-tube is long.

PressureVessel.note: Thicker walled than an atmospheric tank of the same envelope, hence the higher density.

ProcessColumn.note: Slender and tall; internals (trays or packing) add to the shell mass. NB a single column makes an auto-generated deck very tall unless the layout is given an explicit deck_height.

ProcessEquipment.note: The catch-all. Every Plant/ProcessEquipment class inherits this when nothing more specific matches, so it must stay deliberately unremarkable: a man-sized box that will not distort a layout.

Pump.note: Pump, motor and baseplate. Matches the create_pump archetype in ada.topo_model.equipment.

Separator.note: Horizontal two/three-phase separator: long in X, feed in, gas and liquid out.

Silo.note: Thin-walled bulk-solids storage; light for its very large envelope.

StationaryTransportSystem.note: Conveyor / lift: a long, light run rather than a compact machine.

Tank.note: Atmospheric storage tank; thin shell over a large volume.

TubularHeatExchanger.note: Shell-and-tube: longer and narrower than the generic exchanger because the tube bundle sets the length.

Vessel.note: The vessel family's own default, between an atmospheric tank and a pressure vessel.

WasteGasEmitter.note: Flare or stack: a narrow column of height, fed from the bottom.
